subject: Maths
central_question: How can we describe, compare, measure, draw, and follow angles by thinking of them as fractional turns in clockwise or anti-clockwise directions?
in_scope_units: Recognising full, half, and quarter turns through body movement, clocks, giant wheels, and everyday objects
Relating fractional turns to right, acute, obtuse, straight, three-quarter, and full angles
Making and using paper fans, straws, cardboard shapes, houses, and gymnasts to identify angle types
Constructing angle-measuring tools by folding circles into eighths, sixths, and twelfths
Estimating, measuring, combining, and drawing angles in terms of fractional turns
Connecting minute-hand movement with fractions of a full turn and elapsed minutes
Following sequences of turns from North, South, East, and West in the Fun with Turns activities
banned_topics: degree notation and formal protractor measurement
classification of triangles and quadrilaterals beyond identifying the angles shown
parallel lines, perpendicular bisectors, and formal geometric constructions
reflex-angle terminology not used in the chapter

known_pitfalls.claim: A quarter turn and a half turn both make a right angle.
known_pitfalls.correction: A quarter turn makes a right angle, while a half turn makes a straight angle.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any angle smaller than a straight angle is acute.
known_pitfalls.correction: An acute angle is less than a quarter turn; an angle between a quarter turn and a half turn is obtuse.

known_pitfalls.claim: The end position alone always tells the direction of a turn.
known_pitfalls.correction: Clockwise and anti-clockwise turns can sometimes end at the same position, so the direction and amount of turn must both be stated.

known_pitfalls.claim: Two acute turns must always combine to make an acute angle.
known_pitfalls.correction: Their total may be acute, right, obtuse, straight, or more than straight depending on their sizes.

known_pitfalls.claim: A 1/8 turn is the same as a 1/4 turn.
known_pitfalls.correction: A 1/8 turn is half of a quarter turn; two 1/8 turns make 1/4 turn.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Statue game and opening clock/giant-wheel examples on pages 32–33: identify full, half, and quarter turns
NCERT straw and paper-fan activities on pages 33–36: connect turn size to acute, right, obtuse, and straight angles
NCERT Angle Measuring Tool and Let Us Think on pages 36–37: build eighth-, sixth-, and twelfth-turn pieces
NCERT Let Us Do Q1–Q5 on pages 38–39: estimate, measure, combine, and draw turns
NCERT Let Us Do Q6 and Which direction? on pages 39–40: connect clock minutes to turns and distinguish clockwise from anti-clockwise
NCERT Fun with Turns Q1–Q2 on pages 40–41: determine ending directions and equivalent ways to face the same place
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The concluding practice consists of Let Us Do Questions 1–6 on pages 38–40 and Fun with Turns Questions 1–2 on pages 40–41.
